newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Anaconda says Glencore takes 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Anaconda says Glencore takes 40 pct.

text.p: Anaconda Nickel NL said on Monday that Glencore Ag would pay US$220 million for a 40 percent stake in the Murrin Murrin nickel-cobalt project in Western Australia.
The company also said that Korean interests had bid for 15 percent of the project.

"Anaconda has received a bid for a 15 percent stake in the Murrin Murrin project from an industrial consortium comprising some of Korea's largest industrial conglomerates, including Hyundai Corp, The Halla Group and Tong Yang Global Corp," Anaconda said.
"The offer is for US$82.5 million, approximately A$105 million including the syndicate's equity finance contribution for a 15 percent stake," Anaconda said.
The Korean offer remained subject to formal documentation and Hyundai and Anaconda were exploring other ways that the syndicate might help the Murrin Murrin project, it said.
Anaconda said one third of the funds from Glencore would be available prior to formal bank finance being committed, which was expected in March 1997.

"With existing commitments to outsource the project's infrastructure, the equity funds of A$280 million (from Glencore) will be more than sufficient to fund the equity requirements of the Project," it said.
The A$780 million Murrin Murrin nickel project is forecast to produce 100 million pounds of nickel a year once it is fully operational in mid-1998.
Anaconda has said that it could expand the project's annual output to 150 million pounds of nickel and 10 million pounds of cobalt.
It has also said initial estimates indicate this capacity could be in place before the year 2000, registering unit capital costs of around US$3.00 to US$4.00 per pound of nickel produced.
Anaconda's shares closed down four cents at A$4.06 on Monday.
